principle.name: Behavior Preservation First
principle.description: Never change external behavior during refactoring. All refactoring must preserve existing functionality exactly as implemented.
principle.rationale: Refactoring is about improving internal structure, not changing what the code does. Tests ensure behavior preservation.

example.scenario: When extracting a method from a long function
example.good: Write tests first, then extract method ensuring all existing behavior is maintained
example.bad: Extract method without tests, potentially changing return values or side effects

principle.name: Small, Incremental Changes
principle.description: Make refactoring changes in small, testable increments rather than large, risky transformations.
principle.rationale: Small changes are easier to test, review, and roll back if issues arise. Each change should be verifiable.

example.scenario: When breaking down a large class
example.good: Extract one method at a time, testing after each extraction
example.bad: Completely rewrite the class in one large change

principle.name: Test-Driven Refactoring
principle.description: Always have comprehensive test coverage before, during, and after refactoring changes.
principle.rationale: Tests provide safety net and confidence that refactoring hasn't broken anything. They also document expected behavior.

example.good: Write characterization tests, then refactor with tests passing
example.bad: Refactor without tests, hoping behavior is preserved

principle.name: Measure and Quantify Improvements
principle.description: Use objective metrics to demonstrate refactoring value and guide decisions.
principle.rationale: Quantifiable improvements help justify refactoring effort and identify successful techniques.

example.good: Measure cyclomatic complexity before and after, report percentage reduction

principle.name: Leave Code Cleaner Than Found
principle.description: Always improve code quality beyond just fixing the immediate issue.
principle.rationale: The "boy scout rule" applies - leave the code better organized and cleaner than when you started.

example.good: Also improve naming, add documentation, and organize imports
example.bad: Only extract method, leaving surrounding code unchanged

convention.description: Names should clearly express what the code does and why it exists.
Each class, function, and module should have one reason to change.

examples.good: Separate validation, processing, and persistence into distinct classes
examples.bad: One class that handles validation, processing, database calls, and UI rendering

convention.description: Avoid deep nesting, complex conditionals, and long parameter lists.

examples.good: Extract complex conditions to well-named boolean functions
examples.bad: Nested if-else chains more than 3 levels deep

pitfall.why_problematic: High risk of breaking existing behavior and introducing subtle bugs
pitfall.correct_approach: Always write characterization tests first, then refactor with tests passing

pitfall.why_problematic: Difficult to review, test, and roll back. High risk of introducing multiple issues
pitfall.correct_approach: Break down into small, incremental changes that can be individually tested

pitfall.why_problematic: Some refactoring techniques can improve readability but hurt performance
pitfall.correct_approach: Measure performance before and after refactoring, ensure no regression

pitfall.why_problematic: Adding unnecessary abstraction or complexity in the name of "clean code"
pitfall.correct_approach: Apply appropriate refactoring for the actual problem, don't add patterns just because they're "good practices"

category.name: before_starting
category.item: Identify specific code smells and improvement opportunities
Plan refactoring sequence with safety checkpoints

category.name: during_refactoring
category.item: Write characterization tests before changing code
Make smallest possible change that addresses the issue
Run tests after each change to verify behavior
Update documentation and comments to reflect changes

category.name: before_completion
category.item: All tests pass with no regressions
Code follows SOLID principles and project patterns
Code is cleaner and more maintainable than found
